text:
alex cho: quick question — proposing a small refactor for rollout/fallback responsibilities. thinking: keep router dumb (pure routing + fast heuristics) and push complex scoring & decisioning to a central "policy engine". thoughts?

maria nguyen: curious — tilt toward central makes sense for consistency, but worried about latency blast for hot paths.
jordan lee: agree with maria. fallback must be sub-100ms for interactive routes. central eval + cache maybe?
samir patel: can we do hybrid? router uses cached decisions + simple local checks, policy engine recalcs and pushes deltas.
alex cho: that was my idea: local short-circuit rules for immediate failover, policy engine owns scoring, telemetry, and cool-down.
maria nguyen: key questions: 1) what lives in config vs runtime signals, 2) contract between router and policy engine, 3) ownership of canary credits.
jordan lee: i propose contract: router exposes `route_ctx` (tenant, model_id, region, p50/p95 history) -> policy returns `{variant, weight, ttl_ms, reason}`. minimal surface.
samir patel: +1. TTL lets router cache. also allow `force_probe=true` if policy wants a live check.
alex cho: good. example proto-ish:
```
request RouteDecision(RouteCtx) returns (Decision) {
  message RouteCtx { string tenant = 1; string model = 2; string region = 3; map<string,double> stats = 4; }
  message Decision { string variant = 1; double weight = 2; int64 ttl_ms = 3; string reason = 4; }
}
```
maria nguyen: what about A/B vs canary? policy engine should support both; canary crediting tracked per-tenant + global pool. if credit exhausted, fallback to safe variant.
jordan lee: telemetry gating: decisions should include an `safety_score` and policy engine should emit events when safety_score crosses thresholds. this lets SRE create alerts and automated rollbacks.
samir patel: rollbacks: prefer automatic soft-fallback (gradual weight move) over immediate full-swap. router should support weight smoothing over N seconds.
alex cho: agreed. config example for smoothing: `smooth_window_sec: 30, step_pct: 5` in rollout plan.
maria nguyen: question on failure modes: if policy engine is unreachable, router must fallback to last-known cached decision or a tenant baseline. must prefer availability.
jordan lee: yes — fallback hierarchy: 1) live decision, 2) cached decision, 3) tenant baseline, 4) global safe variant. document this in runbook.
samir patel: perf note: policy engine queries must be batched/async for high QPS. router should not block — return cached or enqueue update.
alex cho: ops question: how do we surface reasoning? need traces: every decision should emit a small trace event with reason and safety_score. deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary-policy-v2 -> staging.
maria nguyen: also add audit logs for per-tenant credit consumption. regulatory customers will ask.
jordan lee: actionable TODOs: 1) draft policy proto (alex), 2) router cache behavior + smoothing API (samir), 3) telemetry/safety_score schema (maria), 4) runbook for policy unavailability (jordan).
alex cho: i'll open RFC follow-up with the proto + timing constraints. aim to iterate in next week.
samir patel: ok to start a tiny spike: implement local short-circuit and TTL cache in router; fake policy engine that returns decisions for testing.
maria nguyen: thumbs up. also will sketch the safety_score thresholds for auto-soft-fallback vs immediate rollback. :thumbsup:
jordan lee: thanks — this avoids moving all logic into the router and keeps route latency predictable. good compromise.
alex cho: great thread. i'll post RFC link when created.
